paragraphs: Event cameras capture visual information with fine timing and low latency, but turning their output into useful representations remains challenging. The paper argues that existing deep learning approaches depend heavily on how event data is structured, which can weaken stability and transfer across tasks. It proposes a representation framework inspired by the brain’s dorsal visual pathway.

The framework uses a Continuous-coupled Neural Network to translate event sequences into dynamical signals. Sequences whose polarity stays unchanged produce periodic signals, while sequences with changing polarity produce chaotic signals. Continuous wavelet transforms then analyze the changing states of the network’s neurons, creating higher-order representations of the event stream.

The authors combine these representations with conventional classification networks and report state-of-the-art accuracy of 84.3% on N-Caltech101 and 99.9% on N-CARS. They also report improved generalization and stability of event representations. The contribution is therefore a way to organize event information through neural dynamics, with classification results supporting its usefulness as an input representation.
icml-2025-a-chaotic-dynamics-framework-i.tldr: A brain-inspired framework converts event-camera streams into dynamical signals, improving their representation and reported object-classification performance.

paragraphs: Spoken language models often turn continuous speech into discrete tokens so they can generate speech autoregressively. However, tokens derived from self-supervised models tend to preserve linguistic content more strongly than prosody. A model can therefore retain information about what is said while losing information that contributes to how natural the resulting speech sounds.

Existing methods supplement these semantic tokens with pitch features, but the paper argues that pitch captures only part of the relevant information. Choosing additional features by hand also requires careful engineering. The proposed variational framework instead learns continuous speech attributes automatically and uses them to enrich the semantic tokens through an end-to-end approach.

This changes the representation-learning problem: the system learns which continuous attributes to encode instead of relying on a manually selected feature set. Human raters preferred the speech continuations produced by the proposed approach. That finding supports its intended benefit for perceived naturalness, while the removal of manual feature extraction makes the representation process less dependent on hand-engineered choices.
icml-2025-a-variational-framework-for-im.tldr: A variational framework automatically enriches speech tokens with continuous attributes, producing speech continuations preferred by human raters.

paragraphs: Retrieval-augmented generation combines a retriever with a language model, but those components are often developed independently. Finding documents and generating a useful answer are related tasks, yet the two components may not communicate effectively. C-3PO addresses that coordination problem through a lightweight system positioned between them.

The framework uses three specialized agents to decide whether retrieval is needed, formulate useful queries, and select information suited to the language model. Its inspiration is the repeated query-and-review process people use when searching. Because these responsibilities sit in an intermediate system, the approach can optimize the retrieval pipeline without modifying either the retriever or the language model.

Training coordinated agents also requires deciding how their individual choices contributed to an outcome. The authors introduce tree-structured rollouts for assigning reward credit during reinforcement learning. Experiments within and outside the training distribution show significant improvements in RAG performance and strong generalization. These results support the value of improving communication between components while retaining plug-and-play flexibility.
icml-2025-c-3po-compact-plug-and-play-pr.tldr: C-3PO coordinates retrieval decisions, queries, and information selection through three lightweight agents without changing the retriever or language model.

paragraphs: CLIP learns visual representations by aligning images with their accompanying text. This image-level supervision has made it useful across many applications, including as the visual component of multimodal language models. However, an image-wide description may not provide enough supervision for tasks that require understanding a particular region.

CLOC adds region-text contrastive training and supporting modules to improve this localization capability. Its central representation idea is a promptable embedding: an image representation that can be readily transformed into a representation of a specific region when given spatial hints. This connects whole-image encoding with the more detailed information needed to identify or discuss localized content.

To support training at scale, the authors develop a captioning framework that generates visually enriched labels tied to spatial regions. Scaling to billions of annotated images produces high-quality regional embeddings for recognition and retrieval. The paper also presents CLOC as a drop-in CLIP replacement for multimodal language models, with particular benefits for referring and grounding tasks that connect language to image locations.
icml-2025-contrastive-localized-language.tldr: CLOC extends image-text pretraining with region-level supervision and promptable embeddings to improve localized visual understanding.

paragraphs: Urban region embeddings represent areas of a city in a form that prediction models can use. When each city is modeled separately, however, its embedding space may organize information differently. This makes it difficult to reuse a predictor trained in one city for another, even when the downstream task is similar.

Consistency Region Embedding, or CoRE, combines region representation learning with alignment across cities. It first creates separate embedding spaces for two cities, then aligns both their broader latent-space manifolds and individual regions at a finer level. The aim is to make the resulting representations compatible and comparable across the city boundary.

This compatibility allows knowledge from a city with abundant labels to support socioeconomic predictions in another city without ground-truth labels there. Experiments show that CoRE outperforms competitive baselines for cross-city knowledge transfer. The result emphasizes that transferring a predictor depends on bringing its input representations into correspondence, alongside learning useful representations within each city.
icml-2025-cross-city-latent-space-alignm.tldr: CoRE aligns urban region representations across cities so predictors can transfer knowledge from label-rich cities to cities without target labels.

paragraphs: Sufficient dimension reduction seeks a smaller representation of inputs that retains the information needed for the prediction target. This paper builds on the potential of support vector machine normal vectors to reveal such representations in both classification and regression. It develops a unified nonlinear reduction framework based on an ensemble of classification problems.

The framework connects to kernel principal support vector machines, which operate in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and can almost be viewed as a special case. The authors extend this direction by using a neural network function class. That choice gives the reduction procedure a more flexible family of nonlinear transformations for representing complex inputs.

The theoretical analysis establishes unbiasedness with respect to the central sigma-field, the information structure relevant to sufficient reduction, and gives a finite-sample upper bound on estimation error. Simulations and real-data analyses show competitive performance, especially with heavy contamination, large samples, and complex inputs. Together, the results connect a flexible neural representation with statistical guarantees for the reduction objective.
icml-2025-deep-principal-support-vector-.tldr: The paper extends principal support vector machine ideas with neural networks for flexible nonlinear dimension reduction backed by statistical analysis.

paragraphs: Density ratio estimation compares how strongly two probability distributions assign density to the same inputs. It underlies tasks involving f-divergences, but existing methods can struggle when the distributions differ greatly or have little overlap in their supports. The paper also identifies instability from time scores that diverge near boundaries.

D³RE addresses these problems through interpolating constructions between distributions. Its dequantified diffusion bridge interpolant combines diffusion bridges with Gaussian dequantization to broaden support coverage and stabilize time scores. A second construction, the dequantified Schrödinger bridge interpolant, adds optimal transport to solve a Schrödinger bridge problem, with the aim of improving both accuracy and efficiency.

The paper provides theoretical results for uniform approximation and bounded time scores, directly addressing approximation quality and the identified instability. Empirical evaluations on mutual information and density estimation show improvements over baselines. The contribution brings distribution overlap and score stability into one framework, rather than treating accurate density-ratio estimation as independent of the path connecting the distributions.
icml-2025-dequantified-diffusion-schrodi.tldr: D³RE uses dequantified diffusion and Schrödinger bridges to improve density-ratio estimation when distributions differ sharply or overlap poorly.

paragraphs: Robot reinforcement learning depends heavily on reward functions that describe which behaviors are desirable. Writing those functions can require substantial task-specific work. Language models offer a way for non-experts to describe goals, but text alone can inadequately represent a robotic task, and choosing the relative importance of reward features remains difficult.

ELEMENTAL combines natural-language guidance with visual demonstrations from users. The demonstrations supply information beyond a verbal description, while inverse reinforcement learning balances feature weights to match the demonstrated behavior. This connects the reward design process to examples of what the user actually wants the robot to do.

The framework also uses an iterative self-reflection loop to refine features, rewards, and policy learning together. The authors report a 42.3% improvement over prior work in task success and 41.3% better generalization on out-of-distribution tasks. These experimental findings support combining visual demonstrations, language, and feedback when learning rewards, particularly where text-only specifications leave important aspects of behavior unresolved.
icml-2025-elemental-interactive-learning.tldr: ELEMENTAL combines language, visual demonstrations, and iterative feedback to learn robot rewards with improved reported success and generalization.

paragraphs: Diffusion policies can represent multiple plausible actions for a visual input, making them useful for complex visuomotor tasks. Their action generation process, however, requires repeated sampling steps. That computational cost makes real-time decisions harder, and existing acceleration methods may require retraining or lose performance when too few steps are used.

Falcon exploits the sequential dependence between actions. Instead of beginning every action-generation process from Gaussian noise, it reuses partially denoised actions from earlier information. It then incorporates the current observation, reducing the amount of sampling needed while maintaining the connection between the generated action and the latest visual input.

The method requires no training and can also be added to existing acceleration techniques. Evaluations across 48 simulated environments and two real-world robot experiments report speedups of two to seven times with negligible performance degradation. These findings support using continuity across decisions to reduce repeated computation, with the measured speed-performance benefit established in the reported evaluations.
icml-2025-falcon-fast-visuomotor-policie.tldr: Falcon reuses partially denoised historical actions to accelerate diffusion policies without retraining, achieving reported speedups of two to seven times.

paragraphs: Visual autoregressive transformers generate images through coarse-to-fine prediction across scales. This paper investigates the expressive capacity behind that approach: which mappings can these architectures represent? Its focus is on theoretical approximation ability, including whether a particularly simple visual autoregressive architecture already has universal expressive power.

The authors establish universality for a single-head model containing one self-attention layer and one interpolation layer. More specifically, they prove universal approximation of word-to-image Lipschitz functions. The Lipschitz qualification restricts the function class to mappings whose output changes are controlled relative to changes in their inputs, and is part of the stated approximation result.

The analysis also shows that flow-based autoregressive transformers inherit similar approximation capabilities. These results provide theoretical support for developing computationally efficient architectures without assuming that greater architectural complexity is always needed for expressive capacity. Their significance concerns what the model family can approximate; the paper uses that foundation to motivate design principles for more sophisticated visual autoregressive systems.
icml-2025-fundamental-limits-of-visual-a.tldr: The paper proves universal approximation of Lipschitz word-to-image functions for a simple visual autoregressive transformer architecture.

paragraphs: In a bandit problem, a learner repeatedly chooses among K actions while learning from limited feedback. Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader is attractive because it can provide a best-of-both-worlds regret guarantee without solving the optimization problem used by Follow-the-Regularized-Leader. However, its geometric resampling procedure for estimating losses carries an average per-round cost of O(K²).

The paper introduces Conditional Geometric Resampling, or CGR, to reduce that bottleneck. It provides unbiased loss estimates for general perturbation distributions while lowering average computational complexity to O(K log K). The regret bounds are preserved, so this improvement targets the cost of obtaining the estimates without giving up the stated learning guarantees.

A biased version also controls worst-case computational cost while retaining the best-of-both-worlds guarantee for a particular perturbation distribution. That distribution-specific qualification matters for the stronger runtime control. Experiments report improvements in both average and worst-case runtime, alongside better regret attributed to more stable loss estimation. The work therefore links computational efficiency with the quality of the feedback estimates used by the policy.
icml-2025-geometric-resampling-in-nearly.tldr: Conditional Geometric Resampling reduces FTPL’s average loss-estimation cost from O(K²) to O(K log K) while preserving regret bounds.

paragraphs: Spatial-temporal forecasting predicts data that varies across both locations and time. Graph neural networks can model these relationships and remain robust to noise, but their computational cost can be substantial. Simpler multilayer perceptrons offer greater efficiency, yet simplifying the architecture can also make predictions more vulnerable to noisy inputs.

The paper investigates whether an MLP can retain efficiency while improving robustness. It identifies what the authors call a dual noise effect in spatial-temporal data and develops a theoretically grounded Robust Spatial-Temporal Information Bottleneck principle. This principle provides the basis for RSTIB-MLP, an architecture and training approach intended to manage the robustness-efficiency trade-off.

The training regime includes a knowledge distillation module to strengthen the MLP’s robustness. Comprehensive experiments show that RSTIB-MLP achieves a strong balance between robustness and efficiency, outperforming state-of-the-art graph-based and MLP-based models in the reported evaluation. The findings support treating robustness as something that can be improved through learning principles and training design, alongside architectural choices.
icml-2025-information-bottleneck-guided-.tldr: RSTIB-MLP combines an information-bottleneck principle with knowledge distillation to improve the robustness-efficiency balance of spatial-temporal forecasting.

paragraphs: Direct preference optimization trains language models using preferences between responses, but the paper argues that its alignment benefits do not fully provide the reasoning advantages associated with reinforcement learning. The proposed method aims to combine preference optimization with a search-like response-generation process while remaining free of reinforcement learning.

The approach learns an additional language model alongside the preference optimization procedure. Its response-generation policy has a stated asymptotic equivalence to AlphaZero-like search, allowing the authors to frame it as neural implicit tree search. The method avoids explicit value and reward models. The asymptotic qualification is central: the theoretical connection describes a limiting relationship between policies.

Experiments evaluate both preference alignment and reasoning. The method outperforms regular DPO variants in human preference alignment and language models using Monte Carlo tree search on mathematical reasoning and planning tasks. These results support the proposed combination of preference learning and implicit search behavior, with the theoretical connection explaining why the additional model is relevant to reasoning.
icml-2025-language-models-as-implicit-tr.tldr: An RL-free preference method learns an additional language model whose generation policy is asymptotically equivalent to AlphaZero-like search.

paragraphs: Historical decisions can determine which examples receive labels, leaving the labeled dataset unrepresentative of the full population. A classifier trained on that subset may therefore face selection bias. This paper studies how variation among multiple historical decision-makers, each using a different decision rule, can help address the problem.

The authors use an instrumental variable framework to analyze whether classification risk can be recovered from the available data. They establish conditions for exact identification, meaning that the population risk can be determined within the framework. When those conditions do not yield exact identification, they derive tight bounds on the possible risk instead.

The proposed unified cost-sensitive learning approach handles both identification settings and aims to learn classifiers robust to selection bias. Theoretical and numerical results validate the method. The distinction between exact identification and bounded uncertainty is consequential: the learning procedure is designed to work with what the historical decision process permits researchers to infer, including cases where risk cannot be uniquely determined.
icml-2025-learning-with-selectively-labe.tldr: The paper uses differences among historical decision-makers to identify or bound classification risk and learn classifiers robust to selective labeling.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts language models save computation by activating selected experts, but storing all those experts still requires substantial memory. Post-training quantization can compress models, yet applying it to MoE models can sharply reduce accuracy and generalization. This paper traces part of the difficulty to how sparse, dynamic routing distributes calibration information.

MoEQuant addresses two forms of imbalance. Across experts, infrequently used components receive too few or biased calibration samples. Within an expert, assigned samples differ in their relationship to that expert. Expert-Balanced Self-Sampling builds a more balanced calibration set using cumulative token probabilities and expert-balance measures. Affinity-Guided Quantization then accounts for expert-sample relationships when evaluating each sample’s influence.

Together, these techniques make calibration sensitive to both expert coverage and the importance of individual samples. Experiments report substantial gains, including more than ten accuracy points on HumanEval for DeepSeekMoE-16B under four-bit quantization, as well as improved efficiency. The findings support tailoring compression to MoE routing and aggregation rather than treating all calibration samples as equally informative.
icml-2025-moequant-enhancing-quantizatio.tldr: MoEQuant improves MoE quantization by balancing expert calibration coverage and accounting for the affinity between samples and experts.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to evaluate several policies using a shared data-collection strategy. Given K policies, the objective is to estimate each policy’s expected total reward over a fixed horizon within accuracy epsilon, with probability at least one minus delta. The central question is how to sample efficiently for all the policies together.

CAESAR first obtains coarse estimates of the state-action visitation distributions of the target policies. This preliminary phase has a lower-order sample requirement scaling approximately as one over epsilon. In the second phase, it approximates an optimal sampling distribution and learns importance-weighting ratios for every policy by minimizing a step-wise quadratic loss inspired by DualDICE.

These ratios allow data from the shared sampling distribution to support simultaneous policy-value estimates. The sample-complexity guarantee depends on horizon, target accuracy, and how each policy’s visitation distribution relates to the optimal sampling distribution. Its leading accuracy dependence is inverse quadratic, up to lower-order and logarithmic terms. The result makes the allocation of samples across state-action pairs central to efficient multiple-policy evaluation.
icml-2025-multiple-policy-evaluation-via.tldr: CAESAR evaluates multiple policies from shared samples by estimating visitation distributions and approximating an optimal sampling allocation.

paragraphs: A nested expectation places one averaging problem inside another. Estimating it therefore requires handling uncertainty at both an inner and an outer level. Standard nested Monte Carlo and multilevel Monte Carlo methods are consistent, but the paper highlights that convergence can demand many samples across those levels, making the overall calculation expensive.

The proposed estimator uses kernel quadrature at both levels of the nested calculation. The authors prove that this construction converges faster than all the baseline methods when the integrands have sufficient smoothness. Smoothness is a substantive condition on the result: the theoretical advantage applies when the functions being integrated satisfy that requirement.

The empirical evaluation covers applications in Bayesian optimization, option pricing, and health economics. Across the reported examples, the proposed approach needs the fewest samples to estimate the nested expectations. The theoretical and experimental findings together suggest that exploiting smoothness through kernel quadrature can reduce the sampling burden of computations that would otherwise require extensive repeated averaging.
icml-2025-nested-expectations-with-kerne.tldr: Nested kernel quadrature improves convergence over baseline estimators when integrands are sufficiently smooth and uses fewer samples in reported applications.

paragraphs: Length generalization means learning from shorter inputs and correctly handling longer ones. This paper studies that ability in an idealized setting through a finite, computable question: how long must training inputs be to guarantee generalization, given the complexity of the target function? It calls this threshold length complexity.

The authors show that the Minimum-Complexity Interpolator achieves optimal length complexity. They also connect the existence of computable bounds to whether language equivalence is decidable for the function class. This implies that context-free grammars have no computable upper bound of the required kind. For deterministic finite automata, the paper instead establishes a length complexity of 2n − 2 for an n-state target.

The main positive bounds concern a subset of C-RASP, a transformer-related function class. One-layer functions with precision T have an O(T²) bound, while two-layer functions with K heads have an O(T^{O(K)}) bound. These results distinguish classes where finite length guarantees can be computed from those where computability itself prevents such a general bound.
icml-2025-non-asymptotic-length-generali.tldr: The paper characterizes computable guarantees for length generalization in an idealized setting and derives bounds for automata and transformer-related functions.

paragraphs: Stratified surveys divide a population into groups and choose how many people to sample from each. When estimating a mean under differential privacy, those choices also affect privacy protection. This paper shows why sampling allocations should account for that interaction: traditional designs that ignore privacy can produce substantially inflated estimator variance.

The authors treat stratified sampling as subsampling, which amplifies privacy guarantees. Groups sampled at different rates consequently require different nominal privacy budgets to achieve the same final privacy guarantee. The proposed design jointly accounts for this relationship while choosing group sample sizes to minimize the variance of the private mean estimator.

The analysis covers the Laplace, Discrete Laplace, and Truncated-Uniform-Laplace mechanisms. The authors establish strong convexity of the variance objective and propose an efficient algorithm that finds an optimal design with integer sample sizes. They also characterize aspects of its structure. The contribution makes privacy amplification part of survey allocation itself, linking the statistical design to the mechanism used to protect responses.
icml-2025-optimal-survey-design-for-priv.tldr: The paper optimizes stratified survey sample sizes while accounting for privacy amplification to minimize private mean-estimation variance.

paragraphs: Model merging combines capabilities from several models into one, reducing the need to retain all their parameters separately. However, the source models’ tasks can compete, so a single merged model embodies a particular compromise. That compromise may suit one user while poorly matching another user’s priorities.

Pareto Merging treats performance on each source model’s task as a separate optimization objective. A parameter-efficient structure produces a set of merged models in one merging process, with each model representing a Pareto-optimal solution for a preference. In this formulation, improving one objective at a Pareto-optimal trade-off requires sacrificing another, giving users meaningful alternatives among competing capabilities.

Users can choose a model from the learned set according to which tasks matter most to them. Experiments show that the method produces diverse trade-offs and higher test accuracy than state-of-the-art merging baselines. The contribution is therefore both a merging method and a way to expose preference-dependent choices that would be hidden by returning only one merged model.
icml-2025-pareto-merging-multi-objective.tldr: Pareto Merging produces a preference-dependent set of merged models in one process, allowing users to choose among task-performance trade-offs.

paragraphs: Relational deep learning turns database records and their relationships into graphs so graph neural networks can make predictions. However, the resulting graphs have structural properties that general message-passing methods may not exploit well. The paper identifies many-to-many relationships as a particular source of modeling inefficiency.

RelGNN introduces atomic routes: simple paths that support direct, single-hop interactions between source and destination nodes. It builds composite message passing and graph attention mechanisms around these routes. The design aims to reduce redundant information processing and emphasize the signals that matter for prediction while respecting the structure inherited from the database.

The authors evaluate RelGNN on 30 real-world tasks in Relbench. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on the vast majority of those tasks, with reported improvements reaching 25%. That maximum describes the strongest reported improvement, rather than an average across tasks. The results support adapting graph computation to relational database structure, showing that how information travels through the graph can materially affect prediction quality.
icml-2025-relgnn-composite-message-passi.tldr: RelGNN uses database-aware routes and composite message passing to reduce redundancy and improve predictions on relational data.

paragraphs: Sparse mixture-of-experts models reduce inference computation by activating only selected experts, but all their expert components still create a large memory burden. This can constrain deployment in environments with limited resources. HC-SMoE addresses that burden by merging experts to reduce parameters without retraining the model.

The framework uses hierarchical clustering based on expert outputs. This organizes experts according to their functional relationships, providing a basis for deciding which components to merge. The authors design the clustering to make merging robust independently of routing decisions. The framework is also task-agnostic, so its merging formulation is not tied to a particular downstream task.

The paper provides theoretical analysis and evaluates the method across multiple zero-shot language tasks using models including Qwen and Mixtral. The reported results show superior performance and support practical deployment. Its central contribution is to use what experts produce as the basis for compression, connecting functional similarity with a retraining-free way to reduce the memory requirements of sparse expert architectures.
icml-2025-retraining-free-merging-of-spa.tldr: HC-SMoE reduces sparse MoE parameters without retraining by hierarchically clustering and merging experts according to their outputs.

paragraphs: Autonomous agents execute sequences of actions, making their safety problem more complex than screening an isolated language-model response. ShieldAgent is designed to check those action trajectories against explicit safety policies. The paper addresses malicious instructions and attacks that can lead agents toward consequences such as privacy breaches or financial losses.

ShieldAgent extracts verifiable rules from policy documents and organizes them into action-based probabilistic rule circuits. For a protected agent’s trajectory, it retrieves relevant circuits and develops a shielding plan. A tool library and executable code support formal verification, connecting policy interpretation to checks on the agent’s planned or recorded behavior.

The authors also introduce ShieldAgent-Bench, containing 3,000 instruction-trajectory pairs spanning six web environments and seven risk categories. Across that benchmark and three existing ones, they report state-of-the-art performance, an average 11.3% improvement over prior methods, and 90.1% recall. API queries fall by 64.7% and inference time by 58.2%. These results support the approach’s measured effectiveness and efficiency in evaluating policy compliance across action sequences.
icml-2025-shieldagent-shielding-agents-v.tldr: ShieldAgent turns safety policies into verifiable rules and uses them to assess and shield other agents’ action trajectories.

paragraphs: Vision-language models process images and text together, but their capabilities can coexist with vulnerabilities that cause safety failures. Red-teaming searches for inputs that expose those weaknesses. TRUST-VLM focuses on making that testing process both more successful at finding failures and more diverse in the successful cases it discovers.

The method uses in-context learning to generate adversarial tests involving both image and text inputs. It also incorporates feedback from the target model to improve test-generation efficiency. This creates an adaptive testing process in which the model’s responses inform the construction of further cases, connecting multimodal testing with feedback-driven refinement.

Experiments show that TRUST-VLM outperforms traditional red-teaming techniques in producing effective and varied adversarial cases. The authors also report that these cases provide actionable insights for improving models. The contribution concerns the quality of the diagnostic process: finding a broader and more useful collection of failures can inform model improvement, while the reported findings establish the testing method’s effectiveness in the evaluated settings.
icml-2025-trust-vlm-thorough-red-teaming.tldr: TRUST-VLM combines multimodal in-context testing with target-model feedback to uncover more effective and diverse adversarial cases.

paragraphs: Classifier-free guidance improves visual generation by using both conditional and unconditional model predictions during sampling. That arrangement adds computational work each time a sample is generated. Guidance-Free Training, or GFT, aims to obtain comparable generation performance with a single model during sampling, halving the computational cost described in the paper.

GFT trains directly from scratch instead of requiring a pretrained guided network for distillation. It keeps the same maximum-likelihood objective as the classifier-free guidance setup and changes mainly how the conditional model is parameterized. Most design choices and hyperparameters carry over, so implementing the method requires only small changes to existing training code.

Experiments cover five visual models spanning diffusion, autoregressive generation, and masked prediction. GFT achieves comparable or lower FID scores and similar diversity-fidelity trade-offs to the guided baselines. These findings support the approach across several modeling families: the reported quality and diversity balance can be retained while removing the need for guided sampling at inference time.
icml-2025-visual-generation-without-guid.tldr: Guidance-Free Training matches reported classifier-free guidance performance using single-model sampling and can be trained directly from scratch.
